text: I note the family history of a sibling dying after liver surgery, which raises concern for a metabolic disorder like galactosemia. I need to rule out serious pathology before assuming this is benign breast milk jaundice, so I will request specific lab work. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Hematocrit: 51%

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs show predominantly unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with no evidence of hemolysis, which supports a diagnosis of breast milk jaundice given the normal weight gain and age. However, the family history of a sibling dying after liver surgery is a significant red flag that requires further metabolic screening to rule out galactosemia or other disorders. REQUEST TEST: Urine reducing substances, Serum Galactose, Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT) activity

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal metabolic screening results effectively rule out galactosemia and other inborn errors of metabolism. Given the infant's age, exclusive breastfeeding, adequate weight gain, and unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, this presentation is classic for breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
